title: Runtime exit-mode Sankey and status-code concordance matrix for inference failures
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a new interactive dashboard that visualizes how individual inference requests terminate (exit modes) across the stack and maps those exit modes to HTTP/gRPC status codes and model-level error types. The goal is to make it easy for SRE/Oncall and Platform teams to quickly identify dominant failure phenotypes (e.g., client timeouts -> gateway 504, backend overload -> 503 with queue-drop, model runtime OOM -> 500 model-exception) and their downstream SLO impact. This integrates tracing hooks, enriched metrics, and logs to produce a Sankey of request flows and a concordance matrix of exit-mode vs status-code vs model-error-tag.
acceptance_criteria: Sankey visualization shows flow from request entry point -> routing layer -> compute pool -> model runtime -> termination node, with counts and p99 latency overlays

Concordance matrix rows: exit-mode categories (timeout, overload, throttled, model_error, bad_request, network), columns: transport/HTTP/gRPC codes and model_error_tags. Cells show absolute counts and percent-of-total with color scale
Tracing hook instrumentation added to router and runtime that annotates spans with exit_mode and model_error_tag when available
Log/metric pipeline transforms (Fluentd/Vector) extract exit_mode and propagate as attributes to metrics backend (Grafana/Tempo/Loki) and to downstream BigQuery for ad-hoc analysis
Dashboard exposes time-range filters, service/route/model selectors, and links to representative traces and PRs for remediation
Documented playbook entries mapping top 5 phenotypes to remediation steps and recommended alert thresholds

review_feedback: SRE: pre-aggregate flows in Influx/ClickHouse to avoid Grafana rendering timeouts for 24h ranges
Runtime: prefer emitting numeric exit_mode codes rather than freeform strings; map codes to human labels in panels
Security: ensure no PII/PII-like payload fields are forwarded in traces; small audit requested (ticket raised)
notes: Trade-offs considered: real-time per-request Sankey is expensive; decision to pre-aggregate by 1-minute buckets and compute Sankey flows server-side for ranges > 1h
Alternate approaches rejected: use only logs -> BigQuery ad-hoc analysis (too slow for oncall)
Next steps: final mapping of model_error_tag list from Research, finish trace tagging in router, and land pipeline PRs. After that, schedule dashboard handoff and oncall training session.
